logp.method_description: Octanol-saturated water (OSW) and water-saturated octanol (WSO) were prepared using analytical grade octanol and 0.25 M aqueous NaCl (to suppress aquation of the Ir complexes). Aliquots of the Ir complex stock solution in WSO were added to equal volumes of OSW, shaken in a VWR mini shaker for 6 h and then left undisturbed for the layers to separate (shake-flask method). The octanol layer was carefully separated into test tubes, dried over Na2SO4 and then analyzed by UV-vis spectroscopy at ambient temperature. The concentrations of the Ir complex in the octanol phase were determined using a calibration curve generated using a standard solution of the Ir complexes (0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 mM) in octanol. The concentrations of the Ir complex in water were calculated by following [Ir]water = ([Ir]total added x V(octanol+water) - [Ir]octanol x V(octanol))/V(water). The log of the partition coefficients (LogP) were calculated using the following equation: LogP = log([Ir]octanol/[Ir]water). The logP values shown represent the average number obtained from duplicate experiments performed in octanol:water (1:2) with a total volume of 12 mL.
